newsitem.title: FINLAND: FIM 6 BLN BUFFER FUND CAN OFFSET EXP PRICE FALL - VATT.
newsitem.headline: FIM 6 BLN BUFFER FUND CAN OFFSET EXP PRICE FALL - VATT.

text.p: A six billion markka buffer fund could cushion the negative effects on jobs by cutting employers' indirect labour costs if export prices fell 10 percent, the Government Economic Research Institute (VATT) said on Tuesday.

"If an agreement on moderate wage policy can be connected to the use of the funds, the sufficient size of buffer funds is about 3-4 percent of the private sector's wage sum, or slightly below six billion markka," VATT said in a statement.
It referred to a new report, assessing the possibilities to alleviate the effects on employment in Finland of so called external shocks, mainly a sudden fall in export prices.
Trade unions have repeatedly said a buffer fund arrangement is necessary for Finland to be able to join EMU.
"As a member of monetary union Finland would not have the possibility of old to use a flexible exchange rate to alleviate disturbances," VATT said.

But if export prices fell with Finland in EMU, it must be possible to improve the competitiveness of Finnish companies by some other means to avoid rising unemployment through corporate sector lay-offs, it said.

"One possibility to achieve flexibility in labour costs in the single cuyrency is to adjust social security contributions paid by employers," VATT said, adding this would eliminate any need to lower nominal wages.

In VATT's model, the decline in corporate sector profitability caused by a fall in export prices could be partly offset by a swift reduction in employers' indirect labour costs. In practice, the flexible element could be their unemployment insurance contributions, the institute said.

"If the system could react quickly, the reduction of employers' labour costs would improve competitiveness immediately and would prevent a significant weakening of employment," VATT said, adding the public sector would not face any other adjustment pressures.
The public sector deficit criterion for economic and monetary union and the attached budget stability pact would not impose restrictions in this respect, the institute said.
If a six billion markka buffer fund were used in full, the impact on public sector finances would be a one percentage point deficit -- or well inside the EMU requirements, it said.

A six billion markka buffer fund could be built up over 10 years by raising the unemployment insurance contribution by 0.3 percentage points, VATT said. A credible financing of a buffer fund system would require that employer contributions are raised as export prices rise.
"In this way, the functioning of a floating exchange rate can be imitated, and at the same time the financing of social security can be secured," it said.
